papers.title: Antibacterial and pro-osteointegrative bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces for oromaxillofacial applications: a systematic review and bayesian network meta-analysis of preclinical studies
papers.abstract: Numerous preclinical studies have investigated bioactive coatings on titanium implant surfaces to enhance antibacterial and osteointegrative performance in oromaxillofacial applications. However, these studies employ heterogeneous experimental methods and biological outcomes, making it difficult to identify which coating strategies hold the greatest translational potential. This systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis (NMA) aimed to rank titanium coating strategies published over the last five years according to their biological performance, using a quantitative statistical framework. Nine coating categories of increasing compositional complexity, ranging from single-component (inorganic, organic, peptides/growth factors) to two-component and three-component formulations combining these classes with each other or with antibiotics, were compared across six biological outcomes in preclinical models. Inclusion criteria followed the PICOS framework for studies published between 2020 and 2025. Three databases were searched according to PRISMA 2020 and its NMA extension. Mean difference (MD) was used for outcomes on a common scale; ratio of means (RoM) when measurement units were heterogeneous. Treatment ranking was estimated using the surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA). Study reporting quality and data completeness were assessed, and studies with insufficient quantitative data were excluded from the quantitative synthesis. Of 143 records identified, 59 met the inclusion criteria and 40 contributed to the quantitative synthesis. SUCRA rankings indicated that three-component hybrid coatings incorporating antibiotics achieved the highest antibacterial performance and osseointegration, while inorganic coatings functionalized with peptides or growth factors demonstrated superior osteogenic differentiation. Organic coatings combined with peptides or growth factors showed the greatest cell proliferation. These findings provide the first evidence-based ranking of bioactive coating strategies for titanium implant surfaces, suggesting a potential advantage of multi-component formulations over single-agent approaches across biological outcomes. The identified compositional complexity gradient may inform the rational design of future multifunctional coatings and help prioritize candidates for further preclinical and translational validation in oromaxillofacial applications.

papers.title: Biomaterials in 3D bioprinting: Design strategies, material-technique interactions, and biomedical applications
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting has emerged as a transformative approach in biomedical engineering, enabling the fabrication of complex, patient-specific constructs through layer-by-layer deposition of biomaterials and living cells. This review critically synthesizes the role of biomaterials in 3D bioprinting by comparing how material properties, fabrication techniques, and biological requirements interact to determine construct performance across different biomedical applications. Unlike many existing reviews that discuss materials, techniques, and applications separately, this review focuses on the coupled interactions between biomaterial chemistry, fabrication methods, and application-specific requirements across multiple tissue systems. Across these applications, no single biomaterial satisfies all design requirements, leading to compromises between mechanical strength, printability, and biological performance. Hard tissue applications prioritize thermoplastic polymers and ceramics for structural integrity, while soft tissue engineering relies on hydrogel-based bioinks. Printing techniques such as extrusion, inkjet, and stereolithography impose constraints related to resolution, viscosity, and cell viability, driving the use of composite biomaterials and hybrid fabrication strategies. Despite significant advances, major challenges remain, including mechanical mismatch, limited vascularization, reproducibility, and lack of long-term in vivo validation. This review highlights 4D printing, smart biomaterials, and artificial intelligence-assisted design as emerging strategies to advance clinically translatable constructs. Taken together, successful bioprinting is governed by coupled biomaterial-technique interactions within specific clinical contexts.

papers.title: Towards Sustainable Interactive Devices: A Literature Review of Biomaterials in HCI Fabrication
papers.abstract: Abstract - Biomaterials are increasingly used in HCI fabrication as alternatives to petroleum-derived substrates, offering new possibilities for low-temperature making, embodied material experiences, and end-of-life pathways that differ from conventional materials. While recent reviews have begun to map adjacent subareas (e.g., biomaterials for eTextiles and critical perspectives on living systems), the field still lacks an integrated account of biomaterials as fabrication practices across interactive systems. In this review, we synthesize prior work to connect four elements that are typically treated in isolation: the biomaterial palette used in HCI, the fabrication techniques that make these materials practicable, the ways biomaterials contribute to interactive functionality (including sensing, actuation, and degradation-mediated unmaking), and the application contexts that shape acceptable lifetimes, care demands, and end-of-life handling. By organizing the literature through these linked lenses, we provide a consolidated map of the design space, surface cross-cutting patterns, and trade-offs that recur across material families and techniques, and articulate implications for more reproducible, comparable, and operational sustainability claims in future biofabrication research.

papers.title: A review of prediction and control methods on welding-induced distortions in large metallic structures
papers.abstract: Welding enables cost-effective fabrication of large structures in shipbuilding, aerospace and automotive industries, but repeated thermal cycles during multi-stage assembly inevitably cause distortions that often exceed design tolerances, degrading structural performance and requiring costly corrections. Despite significant advances in local weld modelling, predicting distortion in large, complex assemblies remains challenging due to interactions among material properties, structural geometry, heat input, welding sequence and restraint conditions, particularly for lightweight, thin-walled high-strength steels and aluminium alloys. This review synthesises research from 2000 to 2025 to assess distortion prediction and mitigation strategies for large metallic structures, emphasising industrial applicability. Thermo-elasto-plastic finite element methods provide high accuracy but at significant computational cost and inherent strain-based approaches offer efficient large-scale simulations but rely on calibration and simplifying assumptions, while local/global methods balance accuracy and computational efficiency. Data-driven surrogate models are emerging for rapid prediction and optimisation. No single approach is universally transferable across structural configurations, with scalability generally achieved at the expense of calibration requirements and application-specific assumptions. Distortion mitigation is most effective at the design stage through welding sequence optimisation and structural planning. In-process techniques such as thermal tensioning and controlled restraint further reduce distortions, while post-welding corrections remain less efficient. The literature is strongly concentrated on conventional structural steels, with only approximately 10% and 1% of the reviewed references addressing large aluminium and high-strength steel structures, respectively. Overall, major limitations concern scalability, standardisation and data availability, highlighting the need for integrated physics-based and data-driven frameworks for efficient large-scale distortion control. papers.title: Advanced Control Strategies to Enhance Stability of DC Microgrids Islanded under Dynamic Conditions
papers.abstract: Abstract Islanding of microgrids leads to unwanted fluctuations in power, voltage, current, and frequency parameters. In this paper, a comprehensive three-level control strategy is proposed to stabilize an islanded microgrid by sending control commands to the distributed generation (DG) units based on inverters. The first level of control involves droop control, which manages the power control. The second control level ensures the stability of the voltage and frequency of the network. To implement this control level, the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) method is used for the DC converter connected to the DG unit, and the Virtual Oscillator Control (VOC) method is employed to control parallel inverters. Finally, the third control level, located at the load side, is responsible for stabilizing the power of the islanded microgrid under varying load conditions, which is implemented using a Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF) controlled by Model Predictive Control (MPC). Sensitivity analysis of the proposed control model is carried out under transient conditions caused by load variations, environmental changes (changes in irradiance levels), and consequently, changes in the output power of the DG units. Simulation results in the MATLAB/Simulink environment show that the proposed control strategy can stabilize the microgrid and minimize the fluctuations of power, voltage, and frequency under various operating conditions.

papers.title: Unlocking feedforward capabilities in Model Predictive Control algorithms to deal with measurable disturbances
papers.abstract: Disturbance rejection is a central objective in process control, particularly when measurable disturbances can be exploited through feedforward action. Although Model Predictive Control (MPC) naturally incorporates disturbance models and prediction capabilities, standard formulations cannot achieve complete disturbance rejection since the cost function penalises control effort. This limitation prevents MPC from reproducing the behaviour of classical feedforward compensators. This work proposes a novel framework to embed true feedforward capabilities within MPC without removing the control effort penalty. The approach introduces a dual-control structure in which two control actions are computed simultaneously: a tracking-oriented action addressing set-point tracking and robustness, and a feedforward-oriented action dedicated to disturbance rejection. Both contributions are combined into a single control signal on which the process constraints are explicitly enforced. The feedforward-oriented action is formulated without penalising control effort, enabling full compensation of measurable disturbances. The methodology is developed for Dynamic Matrix Control (DMC), Generalised Predictive Control (GPC), and state-space MPC. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through simulation studies, including comparisons with standard MPC and classical feedforward schemes. A case study based on a reverse osmosis process shows that the proposed approach improves disturbance rejection while preserving constraint handling and overall control performance.

papers.title: Suction drainage is associated with early hemoglobin decline without detectable clinical benefit after total joint arthroplasty: a propensity score–matched study
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate the impact of routine postoperative suction drainage on perioperative outcomes following primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA) using a propensity score–matched cohort. Methods A retrospective cohort study included 2,339 consecutive patients who underwent primary THA or TKA between January 2020 and May 2026. Patients were categorized according to postoperative suction drain use. Propensity score matching using age, sex, and body mass index, with exact matching for procedure type, yielded 630 matched pairs (1,260 patients). Primary outcomes were postoperative hemoglobin (Hb) change and estimated blood loss (EBL). Secondary outcomes included transfusion, length of stay, and postoperative infectious, wound, and thromboembolic complications. Subgroup analyses were performed according to procedure type, antiplatelet use, and anticoagulant use. Results Following propensity score matching, the suction drain group demonstrated a greater reduction in Hb on POD1 (2.0 ± 1.0 vs. 1.8 ± 0.9 g/dL, p = 0.005), whereas Hb change on POD2 was comparable between groups. Estimated blood loss, transfusion rate, length of stay, postoperative wound complications, thromboembolic events, and acute periprosthetic joint infection were similar between groups. Procedure-specific subgroup analyses demonstrated generally consistent findings in both THA and TKA. Among patients receiving antiplatelet or anticoagulant medications, postoperative hemoglobin decline, estimated blood loss, transfusion rate, and length of stay were comparable between the suction drain and no-suction drain groups. Conclusions Routine suction drain use following primary total joint arthroplasty was primarily associated with early postoperative laboratory differences, without meaningful differences in clinically relevant perioperative outcomes. Level of Evidence: Retrospective cohort study, Level Ⅲ

papers.title: Effects of a Flipped Classroom Approach on Grade 6 Learners' Achievement in Marcotting: A Quasi-Experimental Study in Philippine Technology and Livelihood Education
papers.abstract: Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) is a key element of education in the Philippines, aiming to provide learners with the skills, knowledge, and work attitude needed for daily life and careers (Barcelona et al., 2023; Valle & Valle, 2024). At the elementary level, TLE introduces pupils to agriculture, plant propagation, home economics, and entrepreneurship so they can understand basic livelihood competencies before taking specialized courses in junior and senior high school. The purpose of the revised education program under the MATATAG Curriculum (Department of Education [DepEd], 2024) has been repeated, making the classes focused on the learners, stressing the competencies, and considering local realities. In many classes in the Philippines, TLE is still taught mainly in traditional ways. Teachers conduct lectures, explain, and demonstrate as if they had little time for hands-on practice and face issues such as time limitations as well as difficulties with facilities and lack of training (Barcelona et al., 2023; Espiritu, 2022). This limited peer learning becomes especially problematic when teaching procedures like marcotting (i.e., a specific type of plant reproduction in which branches are attached to the parent plant) (Hartmann et al., 2014).To learn how to conduct marcotting, students must grasp several processes, such as selecting a suitable branch, girdling and stripping the bark, applying a damp rooting medium (including rooting hormone, if available), wrapping and securing the medium, monitoring, and separating the rooted branch. When students have little time left to practice these operations under the teacher's supervision, because the lesson is spent discussing each stage in detail, the tension can be resolved by using the Flipped Classroom model. Flipped Classroom alters the way knowledge is conveyed by shifting its transmission to the time outside of class when brief instructional videos and study materials are used. Classroom time is then available for active, collaborative, and hands-on learning under teacher supervision (Abeysekera & Dawson, 2015; Bergmann & Sams, 2012). According to meta-analyses made on flipping, the approach is indeed effective and shows reasonable evolutionary diversity, but the studies are mostly conducted in the higher education sector and school learning, and there is little data about utilization of the flipped approach among learners of the upper elementary school stage, who are less experienced in planning their own education (Lo & Hew, 2017). This gap has practical and theoretical implications. Practically, TLE teachers need to ensure that their efforts to find appropriate materials are reasonable and satisfactory for students, given differences in home devices and internet access. From the theoretical standpoint, the content of TLE, such as cases on marcotting, serves as a perfect material for testing the argument made by many scholars claiming that the mechanism of flipping leads to better learning because it allows students to dedicate class time to guided performance of certain tasks under the supervision of the teacher (Abeysekera & Dawson, 2015; Mayer, 2021). The present study therefore examined the effect of a four-week flipped classroom approach on Grade 6 learners’ achievement in marcotting, compared with conventional lecture-discussion instruction. Specifically, it addressed four research questions: 1. What were the pre-test achievement levels of the experimental (flipped) and comparison (conventional) classes in marcotting, and were the two classes comparable at baseline? 2. What were the post-test achievement levels of the two classes after four weeks of instruction? 3. Was there a significant change from pre-test to post-test within each class? 4. Was there a significant difference in post-test achievement between the two classes, and how large was the difference? Two null hypotheses were tested at the .05 level of significance. H₀₁: There is no significant difference between the pre-test and post-test achievement of learners within either class. H₀₂: There is no significant difference in post-test achievement between learners taught through the flipped classroom approach and those taught through conventional instruction. Review of Related Literature The Flipped Classroom: Definition and Evidence Base The flipped classroom method reverses established norms regarding teaching. The first introduction to a topic is done before students enter the classroom (usually through videos created or shared by the instructor), and time in class is now dedicated only to activities that encourage learners to assimilate, collaborate, and use the information received (Bergmann & Sams, 2012; Bishop & Verleger, 2013). Tomas et al. (2019) point out that flipping is not a means but a continuum of instruments whose efficacy hinges on learners' preparedness and the ability to connect pre-class and in-class activities. Similarly, Deng et al. (2022) argue that flipped learning should be viewed as student-centered, but as a refined practice rather than simply introducing videos into teaching. According to some studies, flipped classrooms can be said to be effective since meta-analyses carried out in various areas show that learners achieve moderate gains (g = 0.19; Cheng et al., 2019) and substantial gains (g = 0.36, van Alten et al., 2019; g = 0.50, Strelan et al., 2020), but the results vary greatly across studies. The effects become more notable when in-class activities involve active learning and include checks for students’ preparation (van Alten et al., 2019). In the study conducted by Gross et al. Reviews of the advantages and pitfalls that flipping presents highlight students’ awareness, teachers’ workload, and access to technology as problems in the field (Akçayır & Akçayır, 2018; Kapur et al., 2022). Flipped Instruction with Younger Learners Most flipped classroom research has been conducted in higher education, and its findings cannot feasibly be applied to younger learners. In the critical review, K–12 studies by Lo and Hew (2017) reveal generally positive effects while identifying challenges specific to school settings: learners almost never watch the videos; access to devices at home is terribly limited; unfamiliarity with the approach; and the time required for teachers to produce materials. They suggested short videos and simple pre-class tasks to diagnose understanding, with in-class activities following directly from that content. In reports involving lower secondary learners, achievement and engagement increased when these were in place (Ying & Ayub, 2022), and research on blended learning with Grade 6 students indicates that learners' self-regulation and access to resources shape outcomes (Nguyen et al., 2024). Taken together, the findings suggest that upper elementary learners will benefit from flipping only when the pre-class component is short, readily available, and closely linked to classroom tasks. Holik (2019) investigated how the flipping process affected students' performance and engagement in a cooking program in CTE and concluded that it increased performance and class involvement because students arrived in class after seeing the process performed first and were ready to master the procedure in the lab. Research in other subjects that focus on skills learned through demonstration has also shown that watching videos on the topic before the lesson improves students' performance and learning (Elmaadaway, 2018). papers.title: Grape Cluster Inspired Biomimetic Composite Solid Electrolyte for High‐Voltage and Long‐Life Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Solid‐state lithium metal batteries suffer from poor interfacial stability and dendrite growth, primarily limited by the ion transport kinetics and mechanical properties of composite solid electrolytes (CSE). Inspired by the hierarchical grape cluster, we design a biomimetic electrolyte via electrospinning PAN fiber “pedicel” integrated with mesoporous SiO 2 ‐SO 3 Li “grape berry” fillers, followed by in‐situ polymerization. This structure establishes long‐range Li + conduction channels and a robust physical barrier, delivering a high Li + transference number of 0.65, ionic conductivity of 1.44 × 10 −3 S cm −1 at 25°C, and a modulus of 520 MPa. Benefiting from these advantages, the assembled LFP|Li and NCM811|Li cells achieve 88.8% capacity retention after 1000 cycles and 94.3% after 300 cycles, respectively. Moreover, a high‐loading pouch cell realizes an energy density of 414.9 Wh kg −1 /797.8 Wh L −1 and withstands harsh abuse tests. Mechanistically, DFT and phase‐field simulations reveal the dual Li + pathways and TFSI − immobilization enabled by the ‐SO 3 Li groups. Notably, a physics‐informed neural network (PINN) framework decouples interface activation‐aging kinetics and predicts long‐term impedance evolution. This work provides a biomimetic paradigm and data‐driven methods for the design and interface analysis of high‐performance CSE.

papers.title: A comprehensive simulation framework for evaluating U.S. lung allocation policies
papers.abstract: Abstract The rapidly evolving landscape of lung allocation policy, including the recent adoption of the Continuous Distribution framework, demands simulation tools that are both flexible and computationally efficient. Existing lung allocation simulators are often difficult to adapt to new policy designs and can be computationally burdensome when large numbers of replications are needed for uncertainty quantification and optimization. This paper introduces the Modular Lung Allocation Policy Simulation Model (MoLAPS), a high-fidelity, discrete-event simulation framework designed to address these limitations through a modular policy architecture and parallel execution. MoLAPS integrates detailed patient and donor data, dynamic medical status updates, and a predictive organ-offer acceptance model. It is implemented with parallel computing support, substantially reducing runtimes for multi-replication and longer-horizon experiments and enabling the exploration of large-scale policy design spaces. The model features a modular architecture that isolates policy components, including allocation, acceptance, and prioritization rules, allowing policymakers to easily evaluate existing and proposed allocation policies, or hypothetical alternatives. A surrogate-based calibration procedure aligns simulation outputs with national organ transplant data, improving empirical validity. MoLAPS is rigorously validated using prediction intervals, quantile-quantile plots, and Chi-squared tests. Simulation results closely align with real-world data across key performance indicators, including transplant rates, waitlist mortality, and organ nonuse. MoLAPS provides clinicians, policymakers, and researchers with a timely, open, and extensible platform for policy evaluation. By enabling realistic, data-driven assessments of lung allocation strategies, it supports more equitable, efficient, and evidence-based transplant policy decisions.

It is concluded that integrating different fields of knowledge into the teaching and learning of botany contributes to cognitive and social development, transforming scientific documentation into an object of social connection that respects and values the sensitivity and life histories of older adults.

papers.title: Bayesian Deep Reliability Network for dynamic human reliability analysis in high-risk industrial environments
papers.abstract: Abstract Industrial and mining accidents continue to pose significant threats to worker safety and production operations worldwide, with human error accounting for a substantial proportion of high-risk incidents. This paper addresses three critical challenges in contemporary Human Reliability Analysis (HRA): the inability of traditional methods to capture dynamic human-machine-environment interactions, the difficulty in integrating heterogeneous multi-source data, and the lack of interpretable uncertainty quantification in deep learning predictions. To tackle these issues, we propose the Bayesian Deep Reliability Network (BDRN), a novel framework that integrates a Graph Attention Temporal Encoder (GATE) for spatiotemporal dependency modeling, a Multimodal Feature Fusion Network (MFFN) for heterogeneous data integration, and an Evidential Deep Reinforcement Learning (EDRL) module for uncertainty-aware decision support. The proposed model is validated on the Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) accident dataset and the New York City Motor Vehicle Collisions dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that BDRN achieves superior performance with an accuracy of 0.892, F1-score of 0.867, and AUC-ROC of 0.921 on the MSHA dataset, numerically higher than traditional Bayesian network HRA models, LSTM-based sequence models, and Transformer-based classifiers. Furthermore, the uncertainty calibration error of 0.068 confirms the model’s reliability in quantifying decision confidence. This research bridges the gap between probabilistic reasoning and deep learning, providing a practical tool for safety decision-making in high-risk industrial environments.

papers.title: Spatially Programmed 3D‐Bioprinted Tumor–Stromal Assembloids Reveal Progressive Microenvironmental Remodeling and Phase‐Dependent Drug Responses in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Hepatocellular csarcinoma (HCC) progression is driven by dynamic interactions between cancer cells and stromal fibroblasts that evolve with spatial proximity and physical association. However, conventional co‐culture models either combine these populations from the outset or maintain them in permanent separation, limiting compartment‐specific analysis of their progressive interaction. Here, we develop a distance‐programmed tumor–stromal assembloid platform in which tumor and stromal microtissues are bioprinted at defined surface‐to‐surface separations. We engineer a collagen–alginate hybrid bioink that restrains spreading, promotes cell–cell cohesion, and preserves discrete tumor and stromal compartments throughout assembly, while interface angle and neck length quantify structural integration, which TGF‐β1 accelerates. Compartment‐specific tracking resolves a graded E‐cadherin‐to‐N‐cadherin transition within the tumor compartment together with progressive activation and spatial expansion of the stromal compartment. Paracrine signaling, fibroblast activation, matrix remodeling, and drug‐resistance programs predominate at distinct phases, producing phase‐dependent responses to pathway‐specific inhibition combined with doxorubicin. Modular repetition of these units extends assembly across a large spatial field, yielding an interconnected centimeter‐scale array with high viability. This platform couples compartment‐resolved analysis of tumor–stromal remodeling with a scalable route to macroscale tumor tissues.

papers.title: Multiscale technologies and strategies for osteogenic hydrogel microsphere systems: From microscale signal regulation, mesoscale spontaneous assembly, and macroscale technology integration
papers.abstract: Background Conventional bone tissue engineering predominantly relies on static preformed scaffolds that lack dynamic microenvironmental adaptability, failing to recapitulate the progressive, endogenous signal-driven tissue evolution characteristic of natural bone repair. To address critical-sized bone defects and repair failures in complex clinical scenarios, the regenerative paradigm is transitioning from static structural filling toward process-driven organoid self-assembly. Hydrogel microspheres have emerged as versatile modular units for building bone-like organoids; however, a comprehensive engineering framework detailing how these microsphere systems exert continuous regulation across micro-, meso-, and macro-scales to yield stable, functional bone tissue has yet to be established. Technology Originating from bio-interface engineering and granular self-assembly principles, this cross-scale technology platform operates across three interconnected levels: (1) Microscale signal regulation, leveraging cell-material interfacial interactions to program cell fate through spatiotemporal factor/ion delivery, localized metabolic/oxygen support, and mechanosensitive signal initiation. This includes the coordinated activation of mechanical transduction (YAP/Piezo1/RhoA), immunoregulatory (NF-κB/mTOR/PI3K-Akt), and master osteogenic (BMP/Wnt/MAPK) signaling cascades; (2) Mesoscale spontaneous assembly, constructing interconnected granular networks via cellular traction forces and dynamic interfacial crosslinking, characterized by spontaneous functional compartmentalization (dense mineralizing cores and loose vascularized channels) and synchronized degradation-remodeling kinetics; and (3) Macroscale technology integration, combining interfacial adaptive crosslinking, non-invasive physical-field actuation (acoustic, optical, electrical, magnetic, and thermal), fluoroscopic guidance, and AI-driven 4D biofabrication. This enables biomechanical stabilization, wireless deep-tissue energetic stimulation, and patient-specific anatomical conformity with host bone. Results By coupling microscale signal regulation, mesoscale spontaneous assembly, and macroscale technology integration, microsphere systems effectively coordinate early immune resolution, microvascular infiltration, and matrix mineralization to achieve robust bone regeneration. Furthermore, this review critically stratifies existing evidence across in vitro platforms, small-animal non-load-bearing models, and large-animal weight-bearing trials, addressing key translational and regulatory barriers to establish a clear engineering roadmap that systematically links localized interfacial signaling, granular organoid assembly, and macroscopic clinical interventions.

papers.title: Differentiable Agent-Based Modeling for Multi-Echelon Supply Chains: Gradient-Based Optimization of Heterogeneous Policies at Scale
papers.abstract: Global supply chains rely on the interactions of thousands of heterogeneous agents, posing significant challenges for optimization. While traditional optimization often assumes homogeneity to ensure tractability, Reinforcement Learning struggles with sample inefficiency when scaling to high-dimensional state spaces. We propose a Differentiable Agent-Based Model for multi-echelon inventory management. By implementing stochastic dynamics via differentiable tensor operations, we enable direct gradient propagation through the simulation. We validate the framework by recovering theoretical Newsvendor optima without supervision. Crucially, we demonstrate ``Mass Personalization'' by optimizing 10,000 distinct agent policies simultaneously in seconds, achieving a 53% cost reduction compared to scalar baselines. Furthermore, we utilize gradient sensitivity analysis to generate causal heatmaps, accurately recovering inherent lead-time delays from the computation graph. This approach bridges the gap between simulation and optimization, enabling the efficient training of self-correcting Digital Twins.

papers.title: Bayesian transfer for offline Q-learning with multi-task Gaussian processes
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning can benefit from data collected in related tasks, yet indiscriminate knowledge transfer may lead to negative transfer under task mismatch and limited target-data coverage. We propose a target-aware Bayesian transfer framework for offline Q-learning based on multi-task Gaussian processes that jointly model task-specific Q-functions. Source tasks are assessed using target predictive evidence and maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), while posterior uncertainty and behavior-supported action sets guide conservative Bellman updates and policy extraction. To account for the dependence induced by Bellman bootstrapping, we distinguish Bellman innovations from bootstrap errors and establish stability and predictive source-selection results under explicit regularity conditions. We further derive selection-adaptive posterior contraction and offline policy-performance bounds, identifying the structural conditions under which source information can be pooled to achieve minimax-optimal rates in a shared-function Gaussian sequence experiment. Simulation studies with heterogeneous source tasks demonstrate improved target Q-function estimation and reduced material negative transfer compared with indiscriminate source pooling. An application to human decision-making data further shows higher average expected immediate payoff than both target-only learning and matched-size random source selection. These results highlight the benefits of combining target-aware source selection with uncertainty-aware conservative learning for reliable and sample-efficient offline reinforcement learning.

papers.title: CoupledFlow: One-Step Neural Operators for Coupled Multi-Physics PDEs
papers.abstract: This paper introduces COUPLED FLOW, a new neural operator learning framework for multi-physics PDE systems that captures the co-evolution of multiple physical processes by modeling their cross-process interactions. Unlike existing neural operator methods that primarily target single-physics settings, COUPLED FLOW employs a novel structure-constrained flow matching algorithm to learn process- specific mean velocity fields conditioned on the full multi-physics state. This enables fast and accurate one-step prediction of coupled PDE systems that would otherwise require expensive numerical simulations. A key challenge in training COUPLED FLOW however lies in sampling structure-constrained conditional flow interpolants that capture cross-process correlations and serve as training examples for flow matching. To address this challenge, we derive a multi-physics mean-flow consistency identity that characterizes cross-process interactions and defines the structure-constrained mean-flow matching loss. To provide informative training samples for flow matching with this loss, we develop a principled method for sampling correlated conditional interpolants based on posterior multi-output Gaus- sian processes, which capture richer cross-process correlations than the commonly used endpoint-conditioned linear interpolants. We also establish a theoretical re- sult showing that the Wasserstein-2 distance between the predicted and oracle PDE solution distributions is upper-bounded in terms of the structure-constrained flow matching loss and the smoothness of the learned flow. Experiments across diverse coupled PDE benchmarks demonstrate that COUPLED FLOW consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art neural operators and generative PDE solvers.

papers.title: BRACE: Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control for Safe Navigation under Unknown Disturbances
papers.abstract: Disturbances encountered during autonomous navigation generally vary across space, often discontinuously, as obstacles redirect wind and changing terrain alters traction. Tracking controllers typically assume sufficient control authority to mitigate disturbances and maintain safety; the regime where this assumption fails remains underexplored. We present Belief-guided Residual Adaptive Control (BRACE), a hierarchical reinforcement learning (RL) framework for reach-avoid navigation under unknown, bounded, spatially varying disturbances. BRACE infers a disturbance belief from model prediction errors and uses that to condition a high-level policy that adapts the reference trajectory. The policy combines a nominal and a belief-guided residual term, trained jointly with a likelihood-ratio advantage reweighting heuristic. We evaluate BRACE in three simulated quadcopter environments with abruptly switching wind fields, and validate it on Crazyflie hardware with fan-generated disturbances. Across these settings, BRACE improves reach-avoid performance over model predictive control and RL baselines.

papers.title: Sampling-based Model Predictive Control as Sequential Monte Carlo Inference
papers.abstract: Sampling-based model predictive control (MPC) is treated as a family of distinct algorithms: predictive sampling, MPPI, the cross-entropy method, and their biased, colored-noise, and annealed variants all sample control sequences and reweight them by cost. We show a single Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) inference algorithm implements them all, specified by three independent axes: the proposal, the update rule that reduces cost-weighted particles to a nominal plan, and the effective-sample-size threshold for resampling. We evaluate SMC-based planning on MuJoCo non-linear control, open-loop navigation through obstacle fields, 7-DoF motion planning, and non-prehensile push-T, in simulation and on a Franka FR3. Resampling combats particle degeneracy at long horizons. At a 28-knot horizon in our navigation domain it cut the collision rate by 30% over non-resampling baselines. Programmable proposals improve push-T success over perturbative baselines, improving from 1% to 100% in simulation and 10% to 90% on hardware.

papers.title: DreamVLA: From Generated Human Motions to Humanoid Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.abstract: Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies typically depends on substantial robot demonstration data, making human teleoperation a costly and cumbersome bottleneck, particularly for whole-body humanoid interaction. Reinforcement learning in simulation offers an alternative for scaling this data, but designing task-specific rewards remains challenging. To address this, we propose DreamVLA, which uses generated motion trajectories to guide reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation, converting them into reliable task execution trajectories. These trajectories train VLA models in simulation without new task-specific teleoperation data. Our central contribution is a reference-conditioned DAgger distillation procedure: after a failed learner rollout, we restart the RL expert from a sampled learner state with the same reference suffix and aggregate successful corrective trajectories, addressing the distribution shift left by offline imitation. We evaluate picking from a platform, opening a drawer, pressing a button, and walking and picking from a platform, with ablations of DAgger iterations, residual RL, and generated dataset scale. Project website: ember-center-berkeley.github.io/DreamVLA.

papers.title: Neural Operator Surrogates for Landweber Iteration in Solving Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: Neural operators can accurately approximate well-posed mappings, but for unbounded or discontinuous operators, common in inverse problems, we verify that their network parameters often blow up in architectures such as DeepONet and FNO. To solve inverse problems stably, we use Landweber iteration, which requires only a forward map and the adjoint of its derivative (linearisation). To reduce repeated PDE forward evaluations, we replace the forward operator and its derivative with a differentiable neural-operator surrogate. We show that encoder-network-decoder operators, including generalised DeepONets and fully coupled Fourier operators, approximate both the forward map and its derivative. A modified discrepancy principle ensures decreasing error before finite stopping. With a compact preconditioner, the iterates remain in a compact set where accurate surrogates exist, and the stopped reconstructions converge as data and surrogate errors vanish under a regularity condition. We also relate the theory to derivative-informed training along finite directions, showing that the preconditioner determines which derivative errors affect the Landweber iteration update. Experiments on identifying a reaction coefficient in an elliptic equation show that smoothing reduces late-iteration deterioration for less accurate surrogates but slows sharp-feature recovery, and that smaller derivative errors along training directions do not by themselves improve reconstruction accuracy.

papers.title: A Gamified Framework for Conflict-Driven Design: Discovering Strategies for Collaborative Resilience with Multi-Agent Learning
papers.abstract: Conflicting stakeholder objectives make it difficult to coordinate investments in urban resilience. We model conflict-driven urban design as a non-zero-sum digital board game in which stakeholder agents allocate scarce resources and balance individual payoffs against shared urban development and resilience objectives. We use multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) to train policies and examine their behavior across three settings. On a 4 x 4 board, learned policies reach about 84% of the total return found by a simulated annealing benchmark. On an 8 x 8 board with spatial and resource constraints, trained agents favor projects that improve resilience in self-play. In a 12 x 12 simulation initialized from historical maps of Tatsumi, Tokyo, trained agents achieve a mean total score of 452.1, compared with 357.3 for a random-policy baseline across 10,000 simulation runs. Gains in adaptability, sustainability, flood resistance, and greenery come with reductions in vitality and density. A human-in-the-loop interface supports replay and lets participants take over stakeholder decisions, providing a testbed for exploring these trade-offs in participatory urban planning.

papers.title: Trainability-Simulability Tradeoff in Parameterized IQP-based Reinforcement Learning Policies
papers.abstract: Parameterized instantaneous quantum polynomial-time (IQP) circuits generate distributions conjectured to be hard to sample classically. As reinforcement learning (RL) policies, their $2^n$ measurement outcomes are typically mapped to a smaller action space by a classical decoder. This aggregation can mitigate initialization concentration while making the policy classically simulable. We characterize this tradeoff through the decoder's Fourier--Pauli expansion. Under independent uniform initialization, we express policy variance as an exact sum over groups of nonconstant Pauli components with identical active-generator signatures. Each group contributes its squared aggregate coefficient times $2^{-r}$, where $r$ is the binary rank of its active generators. An inverse-polynomial aggregate coefficient with logarithmic rank prevents exponential policy concentration. Sparse Pauli expansions and contiguous action bins permit efficient classical additive estimation of action probabilities. We introduce a majority decoder combining protected low-weight components with exponentially large exact Fourier support, preserving initialization nonconcentration while excluding polynomial-size enumeration of the exact expansion. Numerical experiments corroborate the variance laws. In ten-qubit CartPole experiments, majority achieves higher returns than recursive parity and the tested local readouts, while higher-weight Pauli sectors contribute an increasing relative share of gradient magnitude during training. A complementary 21-qubit block-chain policy outperforms an extensive pool of fully connected classical neural networks in episode efficiency, even though its bounded-width structure permits efficient classical simulation. These results guide decoder design for quantum and quantum-inspired RL, distinguishing policy nonconcentration, learning performance, and classical simulability.

papers.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
papers.abstract: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with readiness and execution evidence recorded separately. WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.

papers.title: A Bayesian oriented exploration and reinforcement learning in continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization
papers.abstract: We propose a new reinforcement learning (RL) framework for the continuous-time mean-variance portfolio optimization with unknown market parameters. To better reflect the impact of improved information of the unknown drift on the degree of exploration, we consider a novel randomization based on continuous-time stochastic filtering. Specifically, we construct a continuous-time analog to Thompson Sampling by treating the unknown drift as a random draw from a generalized sampling distribution parameterized by the filter's posterior mean and variance. The new learning objective measures the tradeoff between the wealth performance and the weighted KL divergence between the policy and the true Bayesian posterior, which transforms the classical feedback control into an information guided stochastic policy. As a result, the degree of exploration endogenously depends on the Reward-Biased Maximum Likelihood Estimation that decays with the shrinking filter's variance. This allows us to devise an efficient model-based learning algorithm in the mean-variance portfolio optimization with theoretical guarantee and superior learning performance.

papers.title: AERO: Adaptive Ensemble-Disagreement Routing for Oracle Feedback in Sample-Efficient Online RLHF
papers.abstract: Aligning Large Language Models (LLMs) with human preferences via Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has driven substantial improvements across a wide range of tasks, but the cost of acquiring preference labels remains the dominant bottleneck in the alignment pipeline. While many recent alignment methods improve sample efficiency through active exploration over candidate responses, they typically query the oracle uniformly across contexts, even for contexts where the learned reward estimates are already reliable enough to provide synthetic labels. We propose Adaptive Ensemble-disagreement Routing for Oracle feedback (AERO), a fully online RLHF algorithm built on a Dyna-style model-based RL architecture, in which an ensemble-based Epistemic Reward Model (ERM) serves both as a reward posterior for exploration and as a learned preference-feedback model for synthetic labeling. AERO uses ensemble vote entropy, a Query-by-Committee disagreement measure, combined with an adaptive thresholding mechanism to decide which contexts require oracle feedback and which can instead receive ERM-based synthetic preference labels, concentrating expensive labels where they are most informative. Empirical results across different model families and scales show that AERO achieves highly competitive alignment performance while reducing the required oracle-query budget compared to online DPO and strong active-exploration baselines.

papers.title: Matchability-Aware Conformal Prediction for Open-Ended Language Model Generation
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) often do not produce calibrated uncertainty estimates for their answers. We propose CAELUM, a framework that builds semantic prediction sets while separating aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty. CAELUM samples answers using an ensemble of clarification prompts, clusters them by semantic equivalence, and estimates the aleatoric and epistemic components via kernel-based von Neumann entropy before calibrating nonconformity scores with split conformal prediction. We use a weight $w_λ(x)=1+U_{\mathrm{ale}}(x)+λ\,U_{\mathrm{epi}}(x)$ to control for the contribution of the epistemic uncertainty of each instance and fit a coefficient $λ^\star$ to minimize prediction set size. When the objective is nonflat and selection is stable across splits, $λ^\star$ could be a diagnostic, where large values may indicate epistemic dominance (retrieve, abstain) and $λ^\star\to 0$ aleatoric dominance (clarify). For individual queries, a log ratio $R(x)$ compares the weighted epistemic component with the aleatoric component. Theoretically, we demonstrate that the coverage is capped by matchability, the fraction of items whose reference answer appears in any sampled cluster. Empirically, this matchability can be predicted from the original question features using a lightweight classifier. We use those predictions to define a stratum and derive a conformal coverage bound within it. Across 30 LLM and dataset combinations (4-32B), mean coverage is 0.74 in the learned stratum versus 0.65 overall, averaged over the 78 evaluations using the learned classifier. papers.title: Dynamics-Informed Action Learning for Goal-Conditioned Latent Planning
papers.abstract: Latent world models enable visual control by planning action sequences in compact representation spaces, but a gap remains between how latent dynamics are learned and how they are used for planning. First, teacher-forced training does not expose the dynamics model to the recursively predicted latent states encountered during planning. Second, sampling-based planners typically initialize action search from goal-agnostic proposals, without exploiting the action-conditioned dynamics learned by the world model. We introduce Dynamics-Informed Action Learning (DIAL) to bridge these two gaps. During training, rollout alignment exposes the forward model to its own autoregressive latent predictions, while multi-step inverse supervision trains a lightweight inverse dynamics head to infer actions from latent-state transitions. We further apply the inverse head to model-generated transitions with its parameters held fixed, encouraging predicted rollouts to retain action-relevant information. At test time, DIAL autoregressively couples the inverse and forward dynamics to construct a dynamics-informed action sequence toward the goal, which initializes the mean of the Cross-Entropy Method (CEM) proposal distribution. The subsequent CEM search then refines this initialization using the standard sampling and updating procedure. Experiments across four visual control benchmarks demonstrate that DIAL outperforms existing latent world models and planning baselines in both standard and long-horizon scenarios.

papers.title: Model-Based Imitation Learning For Monocular Vision-Based Navigation
papers.abstract: Reliable navigation with a single monocular limited field-of-view camera is challenging because the lack of depth measurements and limited spatial awareness complicate collision checking. Existing approaches to tackle these challenges fall into two categories. Model-based planners can incorporate explicit collision-avoidance guidance which leads to better generalization but are often computationally expensive and require manual tuning of the algorithmic parameters. In contrast, end-to-end approaches trained by imitation learning can be flexible but typically encode safety only implicitly and thus can suffer from high collision rates in novel scenarios.   In this paper, we present a middle ground through model-based imitation learning. The model-based part is a learned collision model that can map a sequence of past images and a candidate control sequence to a distribution of worst-case obstacle clearance. This predictive distribution in turn is used to define a collision-risk cost in a trajectory optimization formulation. The imitation component uses human demonstrations to learn scene-dependent balancing of collision risk with other task costs such as goal progress. We also use it to learn the algorithmic parameters (e.g., a warm start) of our optimizer to accelerate the solution process. We show that our approach can demonstrate highly reliable navigation in cluttered environments on robots with different embodiments. We also demonstrate a substantial reduction in collision rate over recent end-to-end and model-based baselines.

papers.title: Confronting Uncertainty in Mechanism-AI Coupled Dynamical Systems via Optimal Transport and Information Geometry: Part I. Distribution Learning
papers.abstract: Mechanism-AI coupled dynamical systems are increasingly used to study complex biological systems. However, uncertainty associated with noisy, sparse, and partially observed data limits their reliability. This paper presents a systematic mathematical formulation for treating these uncertainties from the perspective of optimal transport and information geometry. We formulate the uncertainty quantification problem as the minimization of an energy functional on a probability density space equipped with a Riemannian metric, with the loss evaluated through a differential equation, and give a unified description of the gradient flows of the energy functional under specific metrics, such as the Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao metrics. Furthermore, we present corresponding numerical methods for solving these gradient flows using abstract adjoint sensitivity analysis. The formulation connects a range of Bayesian inference methods for dynamical systems; numerical experiments compare posterior approximation and predictive uncertainty under a common computational budget. Moreover, it also provides a geometric perspective on dynamical modeling and the study of heterogeneity evolution.

papers.title: A Trajectory-Aware Domain-Decomposed Multispace Reduced Basis Preconditioner for Parametric Helmholtz Problems
papers.abstract: Repeated solutions of parametric Helmholtz problems arise in multi-query applications such as sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Classical preconditioned iterative solvers do not automatically reuse low-dimensional structures across parameters. Multispace reduced basis (MSRB) preconditioners can exploit such structures by constructing iteration-specific reduced order models (ROMs) from training data, but storing global iteration-dependent bases incurs substantial memory costs. Building on trajectory-aware MSRB training, we develop a domain-decomposed MSRB (DD-MSRB) preconditioner for parametric Helmholtz systems truncated by perfectly matched layers (PMLs). Within flexible GMRES, each reduced space is trained on inverse-action snapshots along the Krylov trajectories generated by the ROM-based preconditioners applied in preceding iterations. To reduce storage, problem-adapted spatial partitions exploit heterogeneous local snapshot compressibility across the physical interior and the PML. Local basis dimensions in each subdomain are determined greedily under a global snapshot-error budget to balance approximation accuracy and storage. The resulting hybrid solver applies DD-MSRB preconditioning during the initial iterations to capture dominant cross-parameter modes and then switches, when necessary, to a shifted-Laplacian preconditioner to reduce error components poorly represented by the reduced spaces. Numerical experiments on two-dimensional half-space propagation, elliptic-obstacle scattering, and three-dimensional waveguides demonstrate significant acceleration over the shifted-Laplacian baseline and substantial memory savings relative to global MSRB. For the largest waveguide system, with 11.0 million unknowns, DD-MSRB reduces deployed ROM storage by 44.9% and mean online solve time by 30.2% compared with global MSRB.

papers.title: Dynamic State Estimation from Sparse PMUs via Physics-Informed Graph Neural Operators
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a physics-informed graph neural operator for power system dynamic state estimation. From a sparse, intermittent measurement window at a few generator buses, the operator estimates the rotor-angle and speed trajectories of all machines, unmeasured ones included, in one forward pass. A graph-attention encoder processes the measurements, and the swing equations are imposed as a hard constraint or as a soft one with a learned correction that absorbs model errors. It is trained on simulated measurements, without state labels. With several phasor measurement units, masked training hides one from the input but keeps it in the loss. On four transmission systems, simulations show that the operator is the most accurate estimator that neither optimizes per scenario nor uses state labels, except on the smallest system at large model errors, where tuned Kalman smoothers are better. Networks trained on simulated states are more accurate on the two smallest systems but not on the 118-bus system, where the operator is faster and more accurate than hard-constrained moving-horizon estimation. Under model errors, it matches or outperforms an optimization-based benchmark at a fraction of its cost. The results hold for a detailed machine model with exact parameters seen only through voltage phasors.

papers.abstract: Most robotic handwriting rigidly mounts the pen and reduces writing to trajectory tracking. A freely held pen instead couples grasp stability, tip motion, and contact force. We present Grip, Trace, Write, a force-aware simulation environment and learning framework for high-DoF handwriting. A two-branch actor separates pen retention from arm-wrist writing while preserving their closed-loop coupling. Training learns a grasp controller, initializes writing from inverse-kinematics demonstrations by behavior cloning, and improves writing through reinforcement learning with rewards on ink, force, time, and retention. Across diverse tasks, the policy improves completion, precision, force regulation, and efficiency over behavior cloning and inverse kinematics, and generalizes without fine-tuning to unseen English and Chinese content. These results establish force-aware handwriting as a testbed for dexterous tool use.

papers.title: Applied bifidelity material response model construction and uncertainty quantification with a sampling hypernetwork
papers.abstract: Multifidelity modeling offers a practical route to accurate prediction and uncertainty quantification when high-fidelity data are scarce but lower-fidelity data are comparatively abundant. This work develops a bifidelity Langevin sampling hypernetwork framework that constructs probabilistic neu- ral response models by learning a posterior distribution over model parameters rather than a single deterministic fit. The method combines a flexible shared-latent data representation for low- and high-fidelity responses, enabling parameter sharing and transfer learning between the fidelities. We introduce several methodological enhancements to improve the robustness and efficiency of this ap- proach, including stability-promoting drift models, staged and conditional training strategies, adap- tive initialization of Langevin trajectories, and training procedures designed to better exploit corre- lations between fidelity levels. These additions improve convergence behavior, reduce the sampling effort required to obtain representative posterior ensembles, and provide more reliable predictive uncertainty in data-limited regimes. The resulting framework makes more effective use of available multifidelity data while preserving interpretability through the learned posterior structure, yielding improved predictive performance, better uncertainty characterization, and a more stable workflow for constructing uncertainty-aware surrogate models. The method is demonstrated on experimental, high-fidelity simulation and illustrative synthetic data.

papers.title: Tiresias: Towards Language-Conditioned World Models
papers.abstract: World models enable planning through internal simulation, while natural language provides intuitive task specification. Yet, language-conditioned world modeling remains fragmented across domains with disparate action spaces, datasets, and evaluation protocols. We introduce LCWM, a shared task that maps an initial agent-view observation and a language instruction to an action sequence that fulfills the instruction. Its accompanying benchmark, LCWM-Bench, integrates 15 datasets across navigation, robotics, 3D gaming, and driving under a shared action interface and evaluation protocol, pairing 142,987 episodes with 428,961 instructions in three styles. We further propose Tiresias, an agent that plans via selective imagination: a language-conditioned diffusion policy generates candidate trajectories, a trajectory ranker shortlists them, and a video-pretrained world model imagines their visual consequences. A visual ranker evaluates these rollouts, complementing trajectory scores to select the final plan. Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench. Ablations demonstrate the complementary benefits of trajectory ranking and visual verification, while experiments with alternative proposal methods show that the trained rankers remain effective beyond our diffusion policy. Together, LCWM-Bench and Tiresias provide a unified evaluation setting and an effective starting point for studying language-guided planning through world models.

papers.title: SAMBoost: Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting
papers.abstract: We propose SAMBoost (Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting), a gradient boosting method that combines tree-based covariate modelling with a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) latent spatial field through a single penalised objective. At each boosting iteration, the predictor is decomposed into separate covariate and spatial components. The method is motivated by applications in which the spatial effect is not a nuisance to be removed but a quantity of interest that must be recovered alongside the covariates. In insurance, for example, practitioners need both flexible nonlinear covariate effects and an interpretable geographic risk surface that can be reported on its own. Existing approaches often involve trade-offs, offering flexible covariate modelling but no explicit spatial field, rigorous spatial inference with a fixed additive covariate structure, or a combination of both at computational costs that limit practicality for large datasets. SAMBoost addresses these goals within the boosting loop, and the underlying mesh produces a sparse precision structure whose cost is largely independent of sample size. On simulations and on an open benchmark, SAMBoost matches or improves on the predictive accuracy of joint Gaussian process and tree boosting approaches. It is also faster and recovers the spatial field and covariate effects more accurately. When covariate effects include interactions, it outperforms additive Bayesian spatial models. Applied to a flood insurance portfolio with 4.9 million records, SAMBoost trains on the full training set without subsampling and runs about sixteen times faster than a Bayesian reference, with a consistent spatial risk surface. A public Python implementation is available.

papers.title: CPNav: Calibrated Vision-Language Navigation for Object-Goal Search in Unseen Environments
papers.abstract: Directing a robot to locate a target object in unseen environments remains a central challenge in embodied AI. Vision-Language Model (VLM)-based methods provide rich semantic reasoning but often produce uncalibrated and overconfident action decisions. We introduce CPNav, a navigation framework that combines collision-aware planning with statistically calibrated VLM action scoring for map-free object-goal navigation. From RGB-D input, CPNav constructs a navigability map, generates collision-free motion primitives, and queries two VLMs for goal detection and action scoring. The resulting scores are calibrated offline via conformal prediction (CP) using oracle actions obtained through a tree-structured exploration procedure with backtracking, providing finite-sample guarantees at a user-specified risk level. The CP layer is model-agnostic and can wrap any VLM policy. Online, calibrated VLM scores guide action selection, while a tree-structured exploration history records alternative actions and allows backtracking. We evaluate CPNav in both simulation and real-world hardware settings. In AI Habitat simulation, compared with the uncalibrated baseline method, CPNav achieves relative SR and SPL improvements of 6.2% and 11.4% on HM3D v0.2, and 12.4% and 8.8% on MP3D, respectively. In real-world deployment on a modified Hiwonder MentorPi robot, the corresponding improvements in SR and SPL are 24.9% and 15.2%, respectively. Code is available at https://github.com/practice-lab-ucla/CPnav.

papers.title: Clinical Performance of a Contemporary Hybrid Surface Implant System—A Prospective Pilot Study
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Contemporary implant designs incorporating progressive macrogeometry and hybrid surface characteristics are intended to enhance primary stability while supporting favorable peri-implant tissue outcomes. This prospective cohort study evaluated the 2-year clinical, radiographic, prosthetic, and patient-reported outcomes of a contemporary hybrid surface tapered implant system with progressive macrogeometry. Methods: Thirty participants received 31 implants and were prospectively followed. Twenty-nine participants (30 implants) completed the 2-year follow-up evaluation. The study was prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05498662). Treatment protocols, including adjunctive grafting and loading, were selected according to predefined clinical criteria. Outcomes included implant survival and success, implant stability, peri-implant clinical parameters, marginal bone levels, prosthetic complications, and patient-reported satisfaction. Standardized radiographs were obtained longitudinally to assess marginal bone-level changes. Results: No implant failures were observed during the study period, and implant success was 96.7% at 2 years. Mean probing depths remained stable, measuring 2.91 ± 0.91 mm at 1 year and 2.86 ± 1.21 mm at 2 years. Marginal bone levels also remained stable between prosthesis delivery and the 1-year follow-up (mean change: 0.00; p > 0.05) and showed a small coronal shift between the 1- and 2-year evaluations (mean change: −0.17; p < 0.001). Prosthetic complications occurred in 16% of sites. Patient-reported satisfaction remained high throughout follow-up. Conclusions: Within the limitations of this small, single-center prospective cohort study, the evaluated implant system demonstrated acceptable clinical, radiographic, and patient-reported outcomes. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

papers.title: Finite Element Analysis of the Foot and Ankle: A Critical Review of Metatarsal Biomechanics, Hallux Valgus, Fixation, and Plantar Loading
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Finite element analysis (FEA) enables evaluation of internal stresses and strains in the foot that are difficult to measure experimentally. This review synthesizes computational evidence on foot biomechanics, focusing on metatarsal loading and stress fractures, hallux valgus pathomechanics and surgical correction, fracture fixation, plantar loading and footwear, and ligament and soft-tissue mechanics. Methods: This critical review is based on a documented, non-systematic search of Scopus and hand searching. Of 169 records retrieved, 123 were retained and 16 sources were added, with six additional references incorporated during revision, yielding a total of 145 references. Information on model geometry, material formulation, loading and boundary conditions, and validation was extracted. Results: Soft-tissue and plantar-fascia properties substantially influenced predicted plantar pressure and internal stress. Metatarsal loading varied with anatomy, gait phase, footwear, and boundary conditions. Hallux valgus models indicated that osteotomy geometry and displacement can redistribute joint and metatarsal stresses, while minimally invasive fixation constructs often provided predicted stability comparable to conventional techniques. Patient-specific imaging, musculoskeletal coupling, and machine-learning methods are expanding model capability. However, most reported results were deterministic outputs from single-subject geometries, and validation evidence was generally narrower than the clinical decisions for which the models were discussed. Conclusions: FEA provides model-based mechanistic insight into foot loading, deformity, and fixation and can support comparative mechanical evaluation of designs and constructs. Its outputs are hypothesis-generating: no reviewed fixation or footwear ranking has been tested against clinical outcomes, and the results should not be read as evidence of clinical effectiveness. Stronger experimental validation, population-based modeling, uncertainty quantification, and clearer definition of model context of use are required before patient-specific clinical decisions can be supported reliably.

papers.title: Dataset-Dependent Performance of Active Learning Acquisition Functions for Multi-Objective Materials Optimization
papers.abstract: Active learning (AL) promises accelerated multi-objective materials discovery, yet acquisition-function choice is often made without matching dataset, budget, and target metric. We retrospectively compared EI-random, EI-cent, EI-maxmin, and EI-prod on Al alloy, steel, and Cu alloy datasets across 100 randomized cold-start trials, using hypervolume, true Pareto-sample discovery, inverted generational distance, balanced-performance score, and iterations to 95% target. EI-prod is best overall on Al dataset; EI-maxmin improves Pareto-front recovery and convergence on steel and Cu datasets; EI-cent gives limited, inconsistent gains. No strategy dominates all datasets or budgets. These results provide a metric-aware, outcome-specific selection guide: use EI-prod for early balanced candidates, and EI-maxmin for broader Pareto-front exploration. They also warn that similar balanced performance does not ensure equivalent front reconstruction and that dataset-specific rankings should inform, not dictate, AL design in materials screening. This reframes acquisition selection as a decision-making, not universal-ranking, problem.

papers.abstract: This study aims to determine the effect of using the Fizzo application on Indonesian language learning outcomes and to describe students' perceptions of its use among tenth-grade students of SMA Negeri 12 Bone. The study was motivated by the need to use digital technology as a learning medium that supports Indonesian language learning and increases students' engagement in reading. A quantitative approach with a pre-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design was employed. The sample consisted of 35 students of class X.5, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through a multiple-choice test (pretest and posttest) and a Likert-scale perception questionnaire, then analyzed using descriptive statistics, the Shapiro–Wilk normality test, the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test, and descriptive analysis of the questionnaire. The mean score decreased slightly from 92.86 (pretest) to 91.71 (posttest), and the Wilcoxon test yielded an Asymp. Sig. (2-tailed) value of 0.655 (> 0.05). Thus, there was no significant difference between the two tests, which means that the Fizzo application did not have a significant effect on learning outcomes within the short treatment period. A ceiling effect, since most students already had very high initial scores, and the short duration of the treatment are considered to explain this result. Nevertheless, students' perceptions were in the good category, with an average of 77.00%. The Fizzo application therefore has potential as a supporting medium for digital-literacy-based learning if it is implemented more intensively and combined with active learning strategies.

papers.abstract: This paper compares four controllers for cooperative object transport with two omnidirectional robots and soft grippers: a baseline constant conformable fractional function (CFF) controller, a polynomial CFF, a force-feedback CFF (FFCFF), and a model predictive controller (MPC) with admittance-based caging. The problem addressed is simultaneous trajectory tracking, collision avoidance, and contact-force regulation during dual-robot caging. The controllers were evaluated under matched settings, including a common force target for the two force-regulating strategies. The MPC combines a digital twin, a virtual-spring synchronization mechanism, and an admittance law that adapts the formation reference to the sensed force. A repeated-trial experiment on circular and sinusoidal trajectories shows that the MPC reduces the normalized transport position error by 7.7% and 9.0% relative to the baseline, and by 7.6% and 6.3% relative to the FFCFF, and reduces the normalized formation error to 0.178 and 0.197 against 0.926 and 0.797 for the polynomial CFF (Holm-corrected p=0.0003). The caging condition was maintained throughout, and both force-regulating controllers regulated the contact force with the payload: the FFCFF applied firmer contact at low computational cost, whereas the MPC applied lighter contact while achieving the highest tracking and formation accuracy. The MPC met the 100ms control period in 99.9% of the control cycles. The results therefore quantify a trade-off between tracking precision, contact force, and computational demand, and indicate that controller selection should follow the application requirements for force regulation and available computing resources.

papers.title: Impact of Cerium and Gadolinium Doping on the Optical and Magnetic Behaviour of Nickel Ferrites
papers.abstract: The rare-earth substitution is a useful means for controlling the electronic and magnetic properties of spinel ferrites. The nickel ferrite nanoparticles, NiFe2−xRxO4 (R = Ce, Gd; x = 0.000–0.100), were synthesized using citrate sol–gel auto-combustion and calcined at 700 °C. The X-ray powder diffraction showed the cubic inverse-spinel lattice structure of NiFe2O4 with minor secondary phases such as CeO2 and GdFeO3 appearing above x = 0.025. The lattice parameter increased from 8.338 Å to 8.360 Å (Ce) and 8.353 Å (Gd), and the crystallite size decreased from 28.4 nm to 21.5 nm and 22.7 nm, respectively. An increase in Urbach energy, indicating increased structural disorder, and a direct band-gap widening from 2.12 eV to 2.31 eV (Ce) and 2.38 eV (Gd) were found by Tauc analysis of the diffuse-reflectance spectra. From the room-temperature hysteresis loops, it is seen that substitution of Ce3+ ions continuously decreased the saturation magnetization from 48.2 to 38.0 emu/g, whereas substitution of Gd3+ ions gave a maximum value of 52.4 emu/g at x = 0.050 and then gradually decreased. Both dopants caused a decrease in coercivity, which is considered a magnetic softening. Contrasting behaviour is explained in terms of differences in ionic radius, site preference, 4f – 3d exchange, and secondary-phase formation. The compositions around x = 0.05 have the best combination of tunable band gap and increased magnetization.

summary_en.motivation: Rare-earth substitution is explored as a route to tune the electronic and magnetic response of spinel nickel ferrites.
summary_en.method: Ce- and Gd-substituted NiFe2-xRxO4 nanoparticles were produced by citrate sol-gel auto-combustion, calcined at 700 C, and characterized by XRD, diffuse-reflectance spectroscopy, and room-temperature magnetometry.

papers.title: Neuro-Symbolic Artificial Intelligence for Secure, Explainable, and Intelligent Banking and FinTech Systems: Fraud Detection, Credit Risk, Financial Forecasting, and Transaction Security
papers.abstract: The rapid digitalization of banking and FinTech systems has intensified the need for artificial intelligence that is accurate, secure, explainable, and regulation-compliant. Conventional deep learning models deliver strong predictive performance but remain opaque black boxes, while Large Language Models (LLMs) offer powerful unstructured-data understanding yet suffer from hallucination and weak constraint satisfaction. Neither paradigm alone satisfies the transparency and compliance demands of modern financial regulation. This paper proposes the Explainable Neuro-Symbolic Trust Layer (XNSTL), a unified framework integrating LLM-based neural learning with symbolic rule reasoning, financial ontologies, and a regulatory audit mechanism to serve four critical banking tasks: fraud detection, credit risk assessment, financial forecasting, and transaction security. The XNSTL architecture comprises four modules: (i) an LLM-based feature extraction module for unstructured financial data; (ii) a symbolic rule engine encoding AML/KYC, Basel III, and institutional credit policies; (iii) a neuro-symbolic fusion module with confidence calibration and uncertainty quantification; and (iv) an explainability and audit layer generating counterfactual explanations and tamper-proof audit trails. We formalize the four tasks, define a hybrid loss function jointly optimizing predictive accuracy, symbolic constraint satisfaction, and explanation faithfulness, and propose an evaluation protocol using public benchmarks including IEEE-CIS Fraud Detection and Lending Club datasets. The framework is designed to reduce false positives in fraud detection, improve fairness in credit decisions, strengthen forecasting robustness under regime shifts, and enable real-time, audit-ready transaction security, establishing a pathway toward trustworthy and regulation-native financial AI.
papers.venue: Scholars Journal of Engineering and Technology
